description: Profile a window: GDScript function costs, fps, monitors; visual adds CPU/GPU ms per render stage, timeline both over time. Requires run_project with profiling: true. Blocks for `seconds` (default 5, max 30; longer: start_profiler). Times are elapsed, not CPU; never sum totalMs (rows overlap). Returns: warnings first, projectPath, complete, fps, slowFrames, rows, frame, servers, worstFrame, monitors, visual, timeline. Errors if profiling is off, a capture is open or the game exits mid-window.

captureLimit.description: Rows the engine puts in each frame packet, 16..512 (default: 512). Godot selects them by inclusive time, so a lower limit hides cheap functions and sets limitReached.

seconds.description: Capture duration in seconds, greater than 0 and at most 30 (default: 5). The call answers only when the window has closed, and with its waits can take up to 58 s, which the limit keeps under a client's 60 s request timeout. Time spent waiting for the session queue counts against that: a call whose wait plus its worst case would pass 60 s is refused with nothing sent. For a longer capture use start_profiler (up to 60 s) and stop_profiler.

sort.description: Rank by own time ("selfMs", default), inclusive time ("totalMs"), or invocation count ("calls").

targetFps.description: Frame rate to hold the game to (default: 60). slowFrames counts frames whose frameMs exceeds 1000/targetFps, over the capture and per timeline interval. Under vsync every frame lasts the refresh interval: disable vsync, or set targetFps a few percent below the refresh rate.

timeline.description: Also record the capture over time in `timeline.buckets`: per interval the fps, frameMs avg/max, process/physics/script ms, slowFrames, draw calls, render CPU/GPU ms (with visual) and the heaviest functions, server calls or render stages (`top`, named once in `timeline.items`) - where and when frames got slow (default: false). timelineMs, timelineTop, timelineBuckets and track turn it on by themselves; false beside any is rejected.

timelineBuckets.description: Most intervals the timeline reply holds, 4..60 (default: 20). A capture recorded in more is merged: adjacent intervals combine (counts and times add up, maxima stay) and `timeline.bucketMs` reports the width. Implies timeline.

timelineMs.description: Timeline interval in milliseconds, 250..5000 (default: 500). Records at most about 60 intervals (60 s: 1000 ms) and the reply merges them down to timelineBuckets. Implies timeline.

timelineTop.description: Heaviest functions, server calls or render stages listed per timeline interval, 0..10 (default: 3). 0 leaves `top` empty. Implies timeline.

top.description: How many functions to return, 1..100 (default: 20). Also caps visual.areas when the capture recorded render stages.

track.description: Up to 4 NodePath:property values the game samples during the capture (every 250 ms, or half the interval when shorter), placed on the timeline by frame number, e.g. "/root/Main/Player:global_position" - where the player was when frames got slow. Implies timeline. Uses the bridge: drive the game between start_profiler and stop_profiler, not in parallel with profile_project. Collected only while the session that started the capture is current.

visual.description: Also record the editor's Visual Profiler: CPU and GPU milliseconds per render stage (culling, shadows, opaque pass, canvas, ...) in `visual` (default: false). GPU times are null on GLES/web builds of the Compatibility renderer, which time no GPU work; `visual.gpuTimed` is false and a warning says so. A frame holds 256 render markers by default; a scene that needs more makes the engine log an error per lost marker, slowing the game, so the capture switches visual off and its warnings say how to raise the limit.

name: profile_project

gpuMs.description: Null when the renderer timed no GPU work (gpuTimed false).

track.description: Tracked values that changed since the last interval with a sample, by spec: absent means unchanged, null means the value became null. The first sample lists every spec. null here means no sample landed in the interval.

gpuMs.description: Null when the renderer timed no GPU work (gpuTimed false).

cpuMs.description: Null when no render frame was folded (frames is 0).

gpuMs.description: Null when no render frame was folded, or the renderer timed no GPU work.
Null when the renderer timed no GPU work (gpuTimed false).
Null when the renderer timed no GPU work (gpuTimed false).
